summary:
1. Project Overview
«Nasa mission educational project» is an educational tabletop card game (ages 9+) developed by team «Hexagon» (Tengri Adara, Zharkyn, Aizirek, Mubina). Its main objective is to teach players space safety, engineering principles, and real NASA technologies through engaging gameplay focused on resolving space station emergencies.
​2. Game Mechanics & Deck Balance (60 Cards)
Built around authentic mission scenarios, the 60-card Print & Play deck includes:
​20 Problem Cards (#1–#20): Real orbital emergencies (space debris collisions, life support failures, solar flares) backed by verified NASA facts and marked with a red exclamation mark on the card back.
​20 100% Solution Cards: Official NASA engineering technologies and protocols that fully resolve threats, marked with a green checkmark.
​14 Makeshift Tool Cards (50%): Creative crew resourcefulness under limited conditions.
​6 Joke Cards (0%): Humorous cards for discard and dynamic pacing.
​3. Scientific Base & Official NASA Sources
Every scenario and solution is strictly verified using open data from NASA Space Station Research and Technology, Orbital Debris Program Office (and FAQ), Office of Safety and Mission Assurance, and ISS National Lab Technology Demonstrations.
​4. Print & Play Format
The project is packaged into ready-to-print PDFs with a complete rulebook, a summary table of all 20 problems and scientific justifications, printable cards with cutting lines, and double-sided card backs.
details:
«Nasa mission educational project» is an interactive educational card game (ages 9+) designed to teach the fundamentals of space safety, engineering protocols, and real NASA technologies. The gameplay revolves around resolving critical emergency scenarios aboard a space station—ranging from orbital debris collisions and decompression to life support system failures. Players match real space problem cards with 100% verified NASA engineering solutions, makeshift crew tools, or joke cards, taking them on a journey from threat identification to mission success.
The project translates complex scientific data and official space agency protocols into an engaging, hands-on format, fostering critical thinking, engineering resourcefulness, and interest in STEM disciplines among youth. It serves as a ready-to-use methodological tool for schools and space clubs. The development utilized open scientific data and verified sources from NASA (such as the NASA Space Station Research and Technology portal, Orbital Debris Program Office, and ISS National Lab). The team structured a balanced 60-card deck and compiled complete Print & Play documentation in English.
The project's creativity lies in its synergy of tabletop mechanics and strict scientific accuracy, where every problem is backed by real spaceflight facts and solutions are based on active NASA technologies. The team carefully considered ergonomic card design, age-appropriate accessibility (9+), and visual clarity by incorporating intuitive markers (red exclamation marks for problems and green checkmarks for solutions).
